Liam — quick technical note and suggested test plan refinements from the infra/serving side.

TL;DR: Redwood can provide the dedicated two-week pool with the following differentiators you asked about: 
- KV/prefix caching that materially reduces tokens emitted for repeated prompts (we’ll measure delta in token cost).
- Smart routing and graceful degrade: we can route to a slightly smaller model variant automatically if a node preempts; falls back to the last cache snapshot to preserve latency.
- Quantization/config profiles: we’ll propose a quantized model variant that delivers 1.8–2x inference throughput at ~1–2% quality delta for your classification prompts.

Proposed test steps (detailed):
1) Baseline run on hyperscaler endpoints using your prompt set (we’ll capture p50/p95/p99, token-cost, and model-quality on evaluation prompts).
2) Run the Redwood dedicated pool with identical traffic for 48 hours to warm caches, then run sustained concurrency tests for 24 hours at 100/500/800 concurrent sessions.
3) Preemption simulation: take a node offline and observe failover; measure latency and error rate for 30 minutes.
4) Cost delta capture: capture actual token+inference unit cost by scenario and provide a summary savings table.

I attached a concise test-plan PDF (redwood-poc-test-plan.pdf) and a simple bash harness we can run. I’ll also include sample workload configs for your infra team.
